why: defending a mark against an attack under way and watching and repairing it shade into each other when alarms and repairs share one thread.

why.T3-044: an outsider saw the CU mark on the canvas and came into the sub to comment, so the mark led a visitor into the room; it is not members finding their own mark (T3-082) nor a call to place (T3-002).

why.T3-002: these are calls to the room's own members to come and place (logo help, a mini buffalo, claim a place) with coordinates appended; the mark is already chosen, so it is T3-002 rather than a proposal of a mark (T3-033) or a template for everyone (T3-070).

why.T3-054: members invite the community onto pxls.space and report its state, i.e. the work carried to a later canvas (a clone site), not a new spot on the same canvas (T3-022) nor a remake in another medium (T3-057).

multiplacement_log.why_this_one: the material satisfies T3-028's gate: scripts made, shared and rewritten for the room's work (C0637948, C0644753, C0363465, C0293389).
multiplacement_log.dispensable: drop T3-028 if forced to one; the Discord move would still stand but the scripting practice would be lost.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-014's gate does not reach the argument over whether scripts are cheating or common practice; nor does T3-028, which carries only the running of scripts, not the dispute over their fairness.

multiplacement_log.dispensable: drop T3-027 if forced to one; the move and the scripts would still stand but the fairness debate would be lost.

why.T3-009: the bulk marks the room's own work as achieved ('we did it', the final image posted as done, the logo complete).

why.T3-015: moderators sticky a hub, redirect proposals into it and delete duplicates with a pointer to the gathering thread, i.e. canvas talk gathered into one place; removals carrying such a pointer are T3-015, not T3-063.

why.T3-105: posts present the room's presence on the final canvas, i.e. the work kept as it stood as a record.
